test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Index published by NITI Aayog?

options.text: A measure of foreign trade performance
A ranking of states based on progress toward SDGs
A list of public sector enterprises

solution:
The correct answer is __**A ranking of states based on progress toward SDGs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **SDG India Index** is a comprehensive tool developed by **NITI Aayog** to measure and monitor the progress of all **States** and **Union Territories** (UTs) towards achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** set for **2030**.
 
• It was first launched in **December 2018** and has since become the primary policy tool for **data-driven governance** in India, fostering **competitive and cooperative federalism**.
 
• The index evaluates the performance of states across **16 goals** out of the **17 SDGs**, using a set of **113 indicators** aligned with the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)** of the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.
 
• Each state and UT is assigned a **composite score** ranging from **0 to 100**. A score of **100** indicates that the state has fully achieved the targets set for the **year 2030**.
 
• Based on the scores, states are categorized into four groups: **Aspirant (0–49)**, **Performer (50–64)**, **Front Runner (65–99)**, and **Achiever (100)**. ***Hence, the statement describing it as a ranking of states based on progress toward SDGs is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Context:** The **17 Sustainable Development Goals** were adopted by the **United Nations** in **2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure prosperity for all by **2030**.
 
• **NITI Aayog's Role:** As the premier policy **Think Tank** of the **Government of India**, **NITI Aayog** is mandated to oversee the implementation of SDGs and coordinate with **Central Ministries** and **State Governments**.
 
• **Indicators and Methodology:** The index utilizes **secondary data** from official sources like the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)**, **National Sample Survey (NSS)**, and various **Union Ministries**. It provides a holistic view of social, economic, and environmental progress.
 
• **Top Performers (2023-24):** In the **4th edition** of the index (2023-24), **Uttarakhand** and **Kerala** emerged as the joint top-performing states with a score of **79**. **Bihar**, though improving, was at the bottom of the list.
 
• **India's Overall Progress:** The country's overall composite score improved from **60 in 2019-20** to **71 in 2023-24**, showing significant advancement in areas like **Clean Water and Sanitation (Goal 6)** and **Affordable and Clean Energy (Goal 7)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Competitive Federalism:** The index creates a **healthy competition** among states to improve their rankings by implementing better welfare schemes and sustainable practices.
 
• **Localization of SDGs:** NITI Aayog encourages states to develop their own **District Indicator Frameworks (DIF)** to monitor progress at the grassroots level, ensuring that the **"Leave No One Behind"** principle is upheld.
 
• **Goals Covered:** The index covers critical themes including **No Poverty (Goal 1)**, **Zero Hunger (Goal 2)**, **Good Health (Goal 3)**, **Quality Education (Goal 4)**, **Gender Equality (Goal 5)**, and **Climate Action (Goal 13)**.
 
• **Impact of Data:** By highlighting **data gaps**, the index pushes for better **statistical systems** across the country, aiding in more accurate **policy formulation** and resource allocation.
